title: UK retail sales, Great Britain — September 2026 (ONS, 07:00 London / 02:00 ET) — the last consumer-volume print before the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget, and the hardest annual base of the year
source: EST: ons.gov.uk/releases/retailsalesgreatbritainseptember2026, re-fetched direct 2026-09-10 (HTTP 200) — the ONS release page reads verbatim 'Retail sales, Great Britain: September 2026', '23 October 2026 7:00am', 'This release is not yet published', and describes the contents as a first estimate in volume and value terms, seasonally and non-seasonally adjusted, carrying ACCREDITED official statistics status confirmed by the Office for Statistics Regulation. Cadence independently reproduced from the publisher's own previous-releases listing (ten consecutive monthly bulletins, every one a Friday 18-27 days after its reference month ends, Oct-2025 data on 2025-11-21 through Jul-2026 data on 2026-08-21) plus the Aug-2026 release page (2026-09-18 7:00am) — and the September-2025 bulletin published 2025-10-24, the same slot one year earlier. Filed estimate on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: and no slot for the UK Office for National Statistics. The DATE is not in doubt; the label is about the taxonomy
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THE never-assessed INITIAL RESEARCH 2026-09-10, superseding proposals/uk-retail-sales-2026-10-23.from-uk-ppi-2026-10-21.json, read in full first per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md. THE PROPOSAL'S TWO FINDINGS BOTH SURVIVE and one is sharpened. (1) PLACEMENT holds: this is the last UK consumer-volume print before the 2026-10-28 Autumn Budget (five days) and before the 2026-11-05 MPC meeting, and it closes an ONS week this calendar already tracks three times over on 10-21 (CPI, PPI, public sector finances). (2) MISSING DEMAND SIDE holds: this calendar's UK set was all prices, labour and fiscal; nothing tracked consumer volumes. (3) SHARPENED — the proposal asked its own research to reproduce the cadence before relying on it, and it reproduces exactly: ten consecutive monthly bulletins on the publisher's previous-releases listing, every one a Friday, plus the August-data release page reading 2026-09-18. WHAT THE INITIAL RESEARCH ADDED. THE ANNUAL BASE IS THE HARDEST OF THE YEAR AND IT IS KNOWABLE TODAY: in the live index (ONS series J5EK, 'Retail Sales Index (DRSI)', last updated 2026-08-20, fetched 2026-09-10), September 2025 stands at 102.7 -- the HIGHEST single month of calendar 2025 (Jan 99.1, Feb 101.2, Mar 102.1, Apr 102.1, May 100.2, Jun 100.5, Jul 102.1, Aug 101.6, SEP 102.7, Oct 101.9, Nov 101.5, Dec 101.6). July 2026 stands at 103.8, so +1.07pp of the September 2026 annual rate is ALREADY DETERMINED and only two monthly clears remain unknown; those clears have run mean +0.25% with a 1.21pp standard deviation over 29 observations since 2024. Base case volume y/y +0.2% to +2.2%, centred ~+1.1%, against +1.6% in July -- a deceleration that is base arithmetic, not a consumer contraction. HOLDING JULY'S RATE WOULD REQUIRE AN INDEX OF 104.4, above June 2026's 104.3 and the highest reading since April 2022 (104.8), 53 months. THE BASE WAS ALSO REVISED UP AFTER PUBLICATION: the September 2025 bulletin (2025-10-24) published +0.5% m/m; the same month now reads +1.08% m/m in the live index. June 2026 went the other way (+1.0% published, +0.68% now). Revisions of 0.3-0.6pp on a monthly rate are routine here and are a kill switch, not a footnote. UNLIKE UK PPI'S SERVICES HALF, THIS PRINT HAS A FORWARD PROXY -- the BRC-KPMG Retail Sales Monitor, whose September edition publishes in the first week of October (BRC's own monitor page states only 'published at least two weeks ahead of official statistics'; no dated schedule was found, so no calendar entry was filed for it). Measured against ONS volumes it is a SIGN indicator and not a LEVEL one: BRC total value minus BRC shop price inflation ran -4.0 / +2.5 / +0.7 / +0.4 / -0.8% for Apr-Aug 2026 against ONS volume y/y of +0.20 / +3.39 / +3.78 / +1.67% for Apr-Jul, a wedge of +4.2 / +0.9 / +3.1 / +1.3pp -- mean +2.4pp, and +1.8pp excluding the Easter-distorted April. NAME COLLISION WORTH ONE SENTENCE IN ANY RECAP: retail-sales-2026-10-15 is the US Census advance print, tiered high; this is Great Britain, eight days later, a different publisher and a different concept (GB volumes, seasonally adjusted, versus US nominal receipts). Tiered LOW and NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED: symbols: [], the tracked universe is eight US mega-caps, and no house playbook is sterling- or rates-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action. Ledger: docs/research/events/uk-retail-sales-2026-10-23.md
